newScenario.recipe: CCR, setpoint 1.2 bar, diluent Tx 15/45, setup cylinder air; 10 min at 30 m; ] for one 0.025 min tick; 5 min at 30 m; B for one tick; ascent to 21 m at 9 m/min.
newScenario.checkpoints: surface, bottom-10min, setpoint-raised (SP 1.3, loop still 1.2), bottom-15min (loop 1.3, ceiling 1.39 m), bailed-out (onBailout true), bailout-ascent-21m (diluent 182.39 bar)
newScenario.whyTheDiluentDiffers: ccr-bailout-30m uses air for both the diluent and the setup cylinder, so no checkpoint could tell which gas a bailout forecast breathes. Here they differ, so the fixture now records legacy's behaviour of forecasting a bailout ascent on the setup cylinder, which is the question #183 raises. The planner parity passes on it because the migration planner reproduces that behaviour.

acceptanceMapping.tankSwitch: trimix-45m-20min: ascent-21m to deco-gas-21m. switchGas(1) after the tick: activeTankIndex 1, one gas-switch event to tankIndex 1, tissues within 1e-9.
acceptanceMapping.setpointChange: ccr-setpoint-bailout-30m: bottom-10min to setpoint-raised. adjustSetpoint(+0.1) after the tick gives targetPo2Bar 1.3 exactly, with no event (legacy records none) and tissues within 1e-9. The following five minutes, replayed at the raised setpoint, match bottom-15min within 1e-9.
acceptanceMapping.bailout: ccr-setpoint-bailout-30m: bottom-15min to bailed-out. bailOut() after the tick: onBailout true, one bailout event, tissues within 1e-9; a second bailOut() returns the same state. The ascent to 21 m, replayed on the model's own breathing source, matches the tissues within 1e-9 and the diluent pressure within 1e-6.
acceptanceMapping.oneDiveNotPossible: The acceptance reads as one dive, but no single legacy dive can hold all three acts: a CCR dive has one open-circuit cylinder in legacy too (TASK-019 loops to tankCount), so a switch is only possible on open circuit and a setpoint or bailout only on CCR. The two recorded dives together cover the three.

orderWithinTheTick: Legacy's updateDiving() runs updateTissues(), then the tank keys (TASK-019), then gas use or updateCCRLoop, then the setpoint keys, then B (TASK-032F). The tick that reads a key therefore breathes the old gas. Each replay advances that tick, then applies the act, which is how the migration client applies an act between whole-second steps. For the five minutes after ], the first tick still breathes 1.2 bar, because legacy raises the loop inside that tick after the tissues.

notComparedAndWhy.switchTickGasBilling: Legacy switches before it bills the tick in which the key is read, so that 1.5 s is drawn from the new cylinder; the migration client bills the step before the press to the old one. That is at most one tick of gas. It is not asserted, and the tissue comparison is unaffected.
notComparedAndWhy.ccrSegmentsUseAnOverride: Before the bailout, the replays pass the loop PO2 explicitly, as tests/parity/tissue-model.test.ts does, because DiveModel subdivides a 6 s legacy tick into 1 s steps and the loop moves inside the tick. After the bailout no override is needed: the breathed gas is constant, so the subdivision is exact, and the gas billing runs too.
